feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV with a clear senior digital communications profile and solid progression within one organization. It reads professionally and is well aligned to strategy/content leadership roles, but it would be stronger with more quantified outcomes, tighter formatting consistency, and a few wording/grammar fixes.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear positioning: the headline, summary, and skills sections consistently support a digital strategy/communications leadership brand.  
- Strong career progression: multiple promotions at NACo show growth, trust, and increasing scope of responsibility.  
- Good credibility signals: named platforms, scale indicators (10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views), and cross-functional leadership make the experience believable and relevant.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more impact metrics: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than results. Include outcomes such as engagement growth, email performance, efficiency gains, cost savings, or adoption improvements.  
- Fix writing/grammar consistency: “more than 12 years experience” should be “more than 12 years of experience”; add serial commas consistently (“content operations, and enterprise web improvement” vs other lists); “cross-channel” vs “Multi-channel” is stylistically inconsistent.  
- Improve structure and reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating these would save space and sharpen focus. Also standardize punctuation in bullets and section formatting.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns well with the CV, but it reads slightly generic and repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening the language and adding more specificity from recent roles would increase impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years’ experience” for cleaner style and correct grammar.
- Replace broad phrases like “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia programs” with “enterprise web, email, social, and multimedia operations” to sound more senior.
- Add a stronger public-sector/association angle, since NACo dominates the experience and is highly relevant.
- Suggested rewrite: Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years’ experience leading enterprise web, email, social, and multimedia operations for mission-driven and public-sector organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel strategy, Drupal-based platform modernization, editorial workflow design, analytics, and digital governance. Known for translating complex policy and technical issues into clear, accessible content and building systems that improve coordination, consistency, and audience engagement.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “workflows and systems” are repeated in Core Competencies/Topline Skills.
- “Advocacy messaging” overlaps with multiple NACo role descriptions; keep it brief here.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this section is too broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT sections. Tightening it to emphasize leadership-level strengths over tools/tasks will improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel, higher-value phrasing: Digital strategy & platform transformation • Cross-channel communications leadership • Editorial systems & governance • Web operations & CMS management • Analytics, reporting & optimization • Workflow architecture & process improvement • Stakeholder alignment & cross-functional collaboration • Policy, advocacy & public-sector communications • Multimedia, livestream & event production
- Change “Multi-channel communication” to “Cross-channel communications leadership” for stronger seniority and grammar consistency.
- Replace “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” with “Stakeholder alignment & cross-functional collaboration” for cleaner, more modern wording.
- Consider ordering by strategic relevance first, then executional capabilities.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Repeats several ideas already covered in the header and Topline Skills, especially digital strategy, multi-channel communications, analytics, and advocacy messaging.
- “Web & CMS administration” and “Workflow & systems architecture” may duplicate Technical + IT unless kept at a higher, non-tool-specific level.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads broad and overlaps heavily with the prior NACo positions and Recent Projects. Make it sharper by emphasizing consultant-level scope, current strategic value, and outcomes.

Suggested edit
- Open with a tighter summary: “Advise NACo on enterprise web strategy, digital governance, campaign platforms, and content operations as an external consultant.”
- Consolidate execution bullets into 2–3 impact-focused lines; e.g., combine systems/workflows/analytics and CMS/front-end/troubleshooting rather than listing each separately.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages supported, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, search improvements, publishing efficiency, or stakeholder adoption.
- Rephrase the AI bullet to show leadership and result: “Led design of an AI-enabled search initiative, defining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, and discovery UX for complex policy content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Campaign and storytelling experiences… custom microsite structures…” duplicates the Recent Projects section; keep this item higher-level.
- “Governance, usability, and operational best practices” overlaps with the 2022–2024 Director role unless framed as post-tenure advisory work.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management details already covered in adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper scope/outcome line: “Directed NACo’s digital media function, leading web modernization, analytics, governance, multimedia production, and multi-channel communications operations.”
- Rewrite bullets to foreground impact: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable results where missing, especially for email/social, video studio, and analytics (e.g., growth, cost savings, faster reporting, improved engagement, reduced vendor reliance).
- Combine softer operational bullets into one concise line: “Established governance, publishing standards, and cross-department planning systems to improve consistency and execution.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the prior Associate Communications Director role; keep this version strategic, not day-to-day.
- Video/programming language also echoes older NACo entries; focus here on building the studio and scaling in-house capability.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles and currently reads as a bridge role rather than a distinct step up. Tighten it around executional leadership, recurring channels, and systems/process gains.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize scope and ownership: “Directed day-to-day digital communications operations across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, supporting coordinated advocacy and member communications.”
- Combine related bullets and sharpen verbs: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more outcome-focused: “Launched and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Replace vague process bullets with one stronger line: “Improved editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing coordination and consistency.” Add a metric if available (send volume, turnaround time, engagement, production cadence).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Strengthened editorial planning” and “improved publishing workflows” overlap; merge them.
- Avoid repeating website/email/social oversight language already used in the Director of Digital Media role.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this skills block is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. It should sharpen the candidate’s senior-level positioning and reflect the most recent enterprise/public-sector leadership work.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with tighter, higher-signal wording tied to current scope:
- Enterprise digital strategy & web modernization
- Editorial governance, publishing workflows & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership (web, email, social, video)
- Public-sector advocacy messaging & stakeholder communications
- Audience-centered content strategy & campaign planning
- Keep wording parallel and concise; avoid vague terms like “focused” where “centered” or “strategy” is cleaner.
- If space allows, prioritize “web modernization” and “content operations” over “messaging,” since those better differentiate senior digital leadership.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” repeat Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” is also echoed in the header and multiple NACo roles.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a generic tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. This topline item should emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities tied to web modernization and platform delivery rather than repeat every platform/tool.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool inventory to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS delivery • Website modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API and workflow integrations • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences”
- Put Drupal first and de-emphasize older/lower-signal platforms unless they are job-target critical; consider dropping either WordPress or SharePoint here.
- Replace “Power Pages” with a broader outcome-oriented phrase only if used meaningfully in recent work, such as “low-code web solutions.”
- If space allows, add one impact cue tied to recent work elsewhere in the CV, e.g. “enterprise CMS modernization for 10,000+ pages.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Nearly all items duplicate the “Technical + IT” section; keep this section strategic and let Technical + IT hold the full tool stack.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also repeats Core Competencies; keep wording distinct.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it reads as a tool list rather than a value statement. It also overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section, so this version should emphasize business impact and decision support.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Analytics strategy, KPI design, executive reporting, SEO/performance analysis”
- Keep only the most decision-relevant tools here; move full platform inventory to Technical + IT
- Suggested rewrite: “Analytics strategy & optimization — KPI design, executive reporting, SEO/performance analysis, and dashboarding across GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, and Microsoft Clarity”
- If space allows, add one outcome-oriented qualifier tied to recent work, e.g. “supporting enterprise web modernization and strategic decision-making”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current item duplicates “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies and nearly all of “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT
- “Leadership reporting” may be stronger as “executive reporting” for clearer senior-level positioning

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid skill cluster, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and multiple NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities and the operational scope behind the work.

Suggested edit:
- Replace task-style phrasing with capability + delivery language, e.g.:
- Broadcast-quality video production & post-production
- Livestream, hybrid & virtual event delivery
- In-house studio buildout & operations
- PTZ camera and multi-camera production systems
- Consider ordering by seniority/impact: studio operations and event delivery before editing.
- If space allows, make one item outcome-oriented: “Broadcast-quality studio and livestream production” to reflect the in-house studio achievement.
- Keep wording parallel and concise; avoid mixing tools (“PTZ camera systems”) with broad functions unless all bullets follow that pattern.

- “Video production and editing” is already strongly evidenced in Work Experience; avoid repeating too broadly.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it’s too generic and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Make this item more senior by signaling depth or primary platforms, especially Drupal, which is central to recent roles.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as: **Drupal (enterprise migrations, modular content architecture) • WordPress • SharePoint • Microsoft Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, prioritize by strength/relevance: put **Drupal** first and consider adding **“10,000+ page migration”** context elsewhere rather than here.
- Standardize naming: use **Microsoft Power Pages** instead of just Power Pages.
- Consider trimming **GitHub Pages** if it was only lightly used; keep this list focused on platforms with meaningful delivery experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This item duplicates the **Topline Skills: Web Platforms & Technical Execution** section almost exactly.
- Avoid repeating platform names in both places unless one version adds context (e.g., primary vs supporting platforms).

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” For a senior digital leader, this item should emphasize implementation scope and modern tools rather than basic languages alone.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Technical Implementation: HTML/CSS/JavaScript • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
- Drop versioning (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless required by the role; “HTML/CSS/JavaScript” is cleaner and more current.
- Consider replacing “jQuery” with “JavaScript/jQuery” only if it reflects recent hands-on work; otherwise remove it to avoid dating the profile.
- If space allows, add a light qualifier for impact: “front-end implementation, tagging, serverless scripting, and deployment automation.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills; keep the stronger phrasing in one place only.
- “Google Tag Manager” may also overlap with analytics/tooling; consider moving it under Data, Analytics & Optimization if that section needs more specificity.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as a generic software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills. Make it tighter and more role-relevant by emphasizing automation builders first and collaboration tools second.

Suggested edit:
- Split by function and prioritize higher-value tools: “Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier | Jira • Asana • Trello | Slack • Teams • Basecamp”
- Consider renaming to: “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools” to better match the content.
- If space allows, add light qualifiers for credibility: “Airtable (system design), Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana, Trello, Slack, Teams, Basecamp”
- Drop any tools you used only lightly; keep the list focused on platforms tied to recent systems/governance work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; avoid repeating those phrases elsewhere.
- Jira/Asana/Trello/Basecamp are similar—listing all four may feel padded unless each was used meaningfully.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it reads as a bare vendor list and misses the scale/ownership already shown in recent NACo roles. It should signal enterprise email operations and member engagement systems, not just tool familiarity.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten/standardize phrasing: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add a light qualifier to show depth without repeating work history: **Enterprise newsletter and campaign delivery** or **Audience segmentation, journeys and newsletter operations**
- Best version if format allows: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp | newsletter operations, audience segmentation, campaign journeys**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding “email newsletters reaching tens of thousands” here; that impact is already covered well in Work Experience.
- Don’t restate broad “multi-channel communications” language already captured in Core Competencies and recent roles.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal and useful scope, but the item is too general and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with concrete outputs if you can quantify them.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize early-career buildout: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital media function, supporting web, email, social and multimedia operations.”
- Add clearer contributions and outcomes: “Supported a major website refresh, improved publishing workflows, and produced recurring digital content including livestreams and weekly video updates.”
- Tighten management phrasing: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “mentored a digital media associate” or “supervised a digital media associate,” if accurate.
- If possible, add 1–2 metrics: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience growth, email/social engagement, or workflow/time savings.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; frame this item as launching or piloting the format rather than expanding it.
- “Strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia” is echoed in later roles; keep this version tactical, not leadership-heavy.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo roles in digital/media. Emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator and tighten the research/program support language.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the unique achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities.”
- Make the second sentence more specific and concise: “Produced digital and multimedia content for member-facing communications, including launching NACo’s first podcast and leading planning, scripting and production.”
- If accurate, add scope or outcome: episode cadence, audience, internal stakeholders supported, or how the podcast/content advanced advocacy/member engagement.
- Consider splitting into 2 bullets for readability and impact rather than one paragraph.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” is too broad and repeats themes covered more strongly in 2015–2024 roles.
- Avoid overemphasizing general coordination; later entries already establish cross-functional leadership more credibly.
